title: D2K-Bench: Can LLM Agents Turn Expert Designs into Efficient GPU Kernels?
title_zh: D2K-Bench：大型语言模型智能体能否将专家设计转化为高效的 GPU 内核？

paragraphs.en: GPU kernels generated by large language model (LLM) agents can remain less efficient than expert implementations, but runtime alone does not reveal how the gap relates to design discovery and implementation. We introduce D2K-Bench , a diagnostic benchmark of 26 tasks and 85 workloads that measures how effectively agents translate expert design guidance into efficient GPU kernels. The guidance covers L1 : high-level algorithmic insights , L2 : dataflow design , and L3 : low-level optimization tricks , including dependencies among these levels. Pairwise runs with and without guidance share task descriptions, workloads, tools, hardware, and a 350-turn budget. Complementary assessments examine independently proposed designs and the design properties implemented in generated code. Across five models on NVIDIA B200 GPUs, guidance raises correctness over 130 model–task pairs from 93.1% to 98.5% and increases the Performance Score over all 26 tasks from 1.46 to 1.95. For the three frontier models with correct submissions on all 26 tasks in both runs (GPT-6-Astra, Claude-Opus-4.8, and GPT-5.6-Sol), geometric mean speedup increases from 1.69 × 1.69\times to 2.49 × 2.49\times . Across all five models, the mean combined implementation score increases from 57 to 70 out of 100. These results show the value of expert design guidance while identifying design properties that remain unimplemented.

paragraphs.en: In modern machine learning systems, GPU kernels usually execute the core computations of machine learning workloads, and their efficiency significantly affects training and inference latency, throughput, and GPU operating cost. Recently, large language model (LLM) agents have offered an effective way to automate GPU kernel development through code generation, compilation, testing, profiling, and iterative optimization [ 1 , 2 ] . Although these development loops can improve performance, the generated GPU kernels could still be less efficient than expert implementations [ 3 ] . Concretely, the LLM-generated kernels and expert implementations could differ in their algorithms, dataflow, and low-level optimization techniques. In this paper, we investigate how effectively LLM agents can translate expert design guidance into efficient GPU kernel implementations.
paragraphs.zh: 在现代机器学习系统中，GPU 内核通常执行机器学习工作负载的核心计算，其效率会显著影响训练和推理的延迟、吞吐量以及 GPU 的运行成本。 最近，大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通过代码生成、编译、测试、性能分析和迭代优化，为自动化 GPU 内核开发提供了一种有效方法 [ 1 , 2 ] 。 尽管这些开发循环能够提升性能，但生成的 GPU 内核可能仍然不如专家实现的版本高效 [ 3 ] 。 具体来说，LLM 生成的内核与专家实现的版本在算法、数据流和底层优化技术方面可能存在差异。 在本文中，我们研究了 LLM 智能体能否有效地将专家的设计指导转化为高效的 GPU 内核实现。

paragraphs.en: Understanding the performance gap between LLM-generated kernels and expert implementations helps target improvements in automated kernel development. The accurately identified gap can inform whether agents need better support for discovering effective designs, implementing and tuning those designs, or both. Algorithmic and dataflow choices can reduce computation and memory traffic, but their benefits depend on the generated code preserving these savings while using GPU resources effectively. Recognizing a promising design therefore does not ensure that an agent can achieve its performance potential. Useful diagnostics should connect an agent’s design choices, their implementation in code, and measured runtime to identify limitations that warrant further investigation. Without such evidence, additional tuning may leave an inefficient algorithm or dataflow unchanged, while further design guidance may fail to resolve implementation limitations.
paragraphs.zh: 理解 LLM 生成的内核与专家实现之间的性能差距，有助于针对自动化内核开发中的改进方向进行定位。 准确识别出的性能差距可以说明，智能体是否需要更好的支持来发现有效的设计、实现这些设计并进行调优，或者两者兼顾。 算法和数据处理流的选择可以减少计算量和内存流量，但其效果取决于生成的代码能否在有效利用 GPU 资源的同时保留这些优化成果。 因此，识别出一个有前景的设计，并不保证智能体能够实现其潜在的性能水平。 有用的诊断方法应将智能体的设计选择、其在代码中的实现以及测得的运行时间联系起来，从而识别出需要进一步调查的限制因素。 如果没有这样的证据，额外的调优可能无法改变低效的算法或数据处理流，而进一步的设计指导也可能无法解决实现层面的限制。

paragraphs.en: However, assessing how effectively agents translate expert design guidance into efficient kernels is difficult since the execution time alone does not clearly reveal which design choices the generated code implements or how well it implements them. An agent must identify an effective algorithm and dataflow, then implement those choices through correct code, GPU execution mechanisms, and tuning. For example, FlashAttention combines online normalization with tiled computation to avoid storing the full attention matrix [ 4 ] . Discovering this design reveals an opportunity to reduce memory traffic; implementing the design further requires coordinated computation and data movement, careful GPU resource management, and tile-size tuning. Runtime alone cannot reveal where an agent falls short. Assessments of independently proposed designs and executable source provide complementary evidence about design discovery and implementation.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，评估智能体如何将专家设计指导有效转化为高效的内核十分困难，因为仅凭执行时间无法明确看出生成的代码采用了哪些设计选择，或这些选择被实现得有多好。 智能体必须识别出有效的算法和数据流，然后通过正确的代码、GPU 执行机制和调优来实现这些设计选择。 例如，FlashAttention 将在线归一化与分块计算相结合，从而避免存储完整的注意力矩阵 [ 4 ] 。 发现这一设计为减少内存流量提供了机会；而要实现该设计，还需要协调计算与数据移动、谨慎管理 GPU 资源，并对分块大小进行调优。 仅凭运行时表现无法揭示智能体在何处存在不足。 对独立提出的设计和可执行源代码的评估，能为设计发现与实现提供相互补充的证据。

paragraphs.en: Existing benchmarks evaluate kernel correctness and performance in different ways: KernelBench evaluates speedup over PyTorch, SOL-ExecBench uses analytical hardware-performance estimates, and FastKernels evaluates generated kernels against production implementations [ 1 , 5 , 3 ] . Prior work also studies optimization guidance and generated code: KernelBench examines hardware knowledge and optimization examples, Hari et al. [2] use Speed-of-Light guidance and LLM-based integrity review, and Shui et al. [6] compare expert-assisted and autonomous kernel development. On the other hand, we focus on a diagnostic approach that can connect task-specific design guidance, pairwise comparisons with and without guidance, and structured assessments of independently proposed designs and generated code. This combination makes the assessed design properties explicit and relates their implementation to correctness and runtime.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的基准测试以不同方式评估内核的正确性和性能：KernelBench 评估相对于 PyTorch 的速度提升，SOL-ExecBench 使用分析性的硬件性能估计值，而 FastKernels 则将生成的内核与生产环境中的实现进行比较 [ 1 , 5 , 3 ] 。 先前的研究也探讨了优化指导和生成的代码：KernelBench 考察了硬件知识和优化示例，Hari 等人 [2] 使用了光速指导（Speed-of-Light guidance）和基于大语言模型（LLM）的完整性审查，而 Shui 等人 [6] 则比较了专家辅助与自主内核开发的方式。 另一方面，我们专注于一种诊断方法，该方法能够将特定任务的设计指导、有指导与无指导条件下的成对比较，以及对独立提出的设计和生成代码的结构化评估联系起来。 这种组合使得所评估的设计特性变得明确，并将其实现与正确性和运行时表现关联起来。

paragraphs.en: Contribution 2. We develop an evaluation protocol that compares kernel performance and design implementation with and without expert design guidance (Section 3 ). The runs in each pair use the same task description, workloads, Triton implementation language, tools, and hardware; guidance provides explanations without expert source code or prescribed tuning parameters. paragraphs.en: Contribution 3. We characterize the benefits and limits of expert design guidance across five models on NVIDIA B200 GPUs (Section 4 ). paragraphs.en: D2K-Bench contains 26 GPU kernel optimization tasks. Each task includes at least two different configurations; we use the term workload to refer to one task with a particular configuration. The benchmark includes 85 workloads in total. The tasks and workloads are carefully selected by experts from systems and specialized implementations such as vLLM [ 7 ] , SGLang [ 8 ] , and FlashAttention [ 4 ] . We select tasks whose expert-written implementations reduce computation or memory traffic through algorithmic transformations or dataflow changes, with low-level kernel optimizations providing further performance gains. The resulting suite spans common kernel development scenarios in LLM training and inference, including attention, mixture of experts, and quantization. Appendix Table 3 summarizes the tasks by operator category along with the representative expert design ideas in each group.
paragraphs.zh: D2K-Bench 包含 26 个 GPU 内核优化任务。 每个任务至少包含两种不同的配置；我们将一个具有特定配置的任务称为“工作负载”。 该基准测试总共包含 85 个工作负载。 这些任务和工作的负载由系统领域的专家以及来自 vLLM [ 7 ]、SGLang [ 8 ] 和 FlashAttention [ 4 ] 等专用实现项目的专家精心挑选。 我们选择的任务是那些由专家编写的实现，通过算法转换或数据流变化来减少计算量或内存流量，而底层内核优化则能进一步提升性能。 由此形成的测试套件涵盖了 LLM 训练和推理中常见的内核开发场景，包括注意力机制、混合专家模型和量化技术。 附录中的表 3 按算子类别总结了这些任务，并列出了每组中代表性的专家设计思路。

paragraphs.en: For each task, we construct a set of shared task files that specify what the agent must implement and how the task will be evaluated. paragraphs.en: Example task of Muon orthogonalization kernel. We enumerate one concrete example, i.e., the Muon orthogonalization that isolates the matrix orthogonalization used by the optimizer, transforming an input gradient matrix 𝐆 \mathbf{G} into an update direction. Figure 1 (a) provides an illustrative summary of these shared task files for the Muon task. Each matrix is normalized in FP32 and then cast to FP16 to initialize 𝐗 0 = FP16 ⁡ ( 𝐆 ( ∥ 𝐆 ∥ F + ϵ ) ) \mathbf{X}_{0}=\operatorname{FP16}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{G}}{(\lVert\mathbf{G}\rVert_{F}+\epsilon)}\right) . The kernel then conducts five polynomial Newton-Schulz updates with FP16 iterates. For a wide matrix, each update step, indexed by k = 0 , … , 4 k{=}0,\ldots,4 , forms the Gram matrix 𝐑 k = 𝐗 k ​ 𝐗 k ⊤ \mathbf{R}_{k}=\mathbf{X}_{k}\mathbf{X}_{k}^{\top} and computes 𝐗 k + 1 = ( a k ​ 𝐈 + b k ​ 𝐑 k + c k ​ 𝐑 k 2 ) ​ 𝐗 k \mathbf{X}_{k+1}=(a_{k}\mathbf{I}+b_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}+c_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}^{2})\mathbf{X}_{k} , where 𝐈 \mathbf{I} is the identity matrix and a k , b k , c k a_{k},b_{k},c_{k} are the supplied coefficients. One workload contains 32 BF16 matrices of shape 4096 × 11008 4096{\times}11008 : each rectangular iterate has this shape, whereas its Gram matrix is 4096 × 4096 4096{\times}4096 . paragraphs.en: Example expert guidance for Muon orthogonalization kernel. We provide the corresponding example of the expert guidance for the Muon orthogonalization kernel. The Muon guidance replaces repeated updates of the large rectangular matrix with composition on smaller square matrices (Figure 1 (b) ). At L1 , the guidance defines 𝐏 k = a k ​ 𝐈 + b k ​ 𝐑 k + c k ​ 𝐑 k 2 \mathbf{P}_{k}=a_{k}\mathbf{I}+b_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}+c_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}^{2} . In exact arithmetic, since 𝐗 k + 1 = 𝐏 k ​ 𝐗 k \mathbf{X}_{k+1}=\mathbf{P}_{k}\mathbf{X}_{k} , steps 0 0 through j j can be composed into 𝐐 = 𝐏 j ⋯ 𝐏 0 \mathbf{Q}=\mathbf{P}_{j}\cdots\mathbf{P}_{0} . The resulting rectangular matrix is then computed as 𝐗 j + 1 = 𝐐𝐗 0 \mathbf{X}_{j+1}=\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{X}_{0} in a single matrix multiplication, avoiding explicit computation of the intermediate rectangular matrices 𝐗 1 , … , 𝐗 j \mathbf{X}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{X}_{j} . Meanwhile, the Gram matrix is updated directly as 𝐑 k + 1 = 𝐏 k ​ 𝐑 k ​ 𝐏 k ⊤ \mathbf{R}_{k+1}=\mathbf{P}_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}\mathbf{P}_{k}^{\top} , rather than recomputed as 𝐗 k + 1 ​ 𝐗 k + 1 ⊤ \mathbf{X}_{k+1}\mathbf{X}_{k+1}^{\top} . This algorithmic transformation preserves the result in exact arithmetic while replacing repeated rectangular-matrix updates with composition on smaller square matrices. At L2 , the dataflow keeps rectangular 𝐗 \mathbf{X} fixed throughout each composition segment, while square states 𝐑 \mathbf{R} and 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} are updated and reused across consecutive polynomial steps. The updated rectangular matrix is materialized only at the segment boundary by applying 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} to 𝐗 \mathbf{X} . Before step k = 2 k{=}2 , the fixed restart applies the composition of steps 0 and 1 to 𝐗 \mathbf{X} , rounds to FP16 , rebuilds 𝐑 = 𝐗𝐗 ⊤ \mathbf{R}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\top} to limit numerical drift, and initializes a fresh 𝐐 = a 2 ​ 𝐈 + b 2 ​ 𝐑 + c 2 ​ 𝐑 2 \mathbf{Q}=a_{2}\mathbf{I}+b_{2}\mathbf{R}+c_{2}\mathbf{R}^{2} for steps 2 through 4. At L3 , the kernel execution schedule respects these data dependencies: square-state matrix-product kernels execute within each segment, and rectangular products apply 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} at restart and final boundaries after the corresponding square-state updates are complete. To avoid redundant arithmetic, symmetric-product kernels compute one triangle and reuse each tile’s accumulator for the original and transposed stores, writing diagonal tiles only once.
paragraphs.zh: Muon 正交化核的专家指导示例。 我们提供了 Muon 正交化核对应的专家指导示例。 Muon 指导将大型矩形矩阵的重复更新替换为对较小方阵的合成（图 1(b)）。 在 L1 处，该指导定义 𝐏 k = a k ​ 𝐈 + b k ​ 𝐑 k + c k ​ 𝐑 k 2 \mathbf{P}_{k}=a_{k}\mathbf{I}+b_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}+c_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}^{2}。 在精确计算中，由于 𝐗 k + 1 = 𝐏 k ​ 𝐗 k \mathbf{X}_{k+1}=\mathbf{P}_{k}\mathbf{X}_{k}，步骤 0 到 j 可以合成成 𝐐 = 𝐏 j ⋯ 𝐏 0 \mathbf{Q}=\mathbf{P}_{j}\cdots\mathbf{P}_{0}。 随后，结果矩形矩阵通过单次矩阵乘法计算为 𝐗 j + 1 = 𝐐𝐗 0 \mathbf{X}_{j+1}=\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{X}_{0}，从而避免了中间矩形矩阵 𝐗 1 , … , 𝐗 j \mathbf{X}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{X}_{j} 的显式计算。 同时，Gram 矩阵直接更新为 𝐑 k + 1 = 𝐏 k ​ 𝐑 k ​ 𝐏 k ⊤ \mathbf{R}_{k+1}=\mathbf{P}_{k}\mathbf{R}_{k}\mathbf{P}_{k}^{\top}，而不是重新计算为 𝐗 k + 1 ​ 𝐗 k + 1 ⊤ \mathbf{X}_{k+1}\mathbf{X}_{k+1}^{\top}。 这种算法转换在精确计算中保留了结果，同时将重复的矩形矩阵更新替换为对较小方阵的合成。 在 L2 处，数据流在整个合成段内保持矩形矩阵 𝐗 \mathbf{X} 不变，而方阵状态 𝐑 \mathbf{R} 和 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} 则在连续的多项式步骤中更新并重复使用。 更新后的矩形矩阵仅在段边界处通过将 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} 应用于 𝐗 \mathbf{X} 来实现。 在步骤 k = 2 之前，固定重启将步骤 0 和 1 的合成应用于 𝐗 \mathbf{X}，四舍五入到 FP16，重建 𝐑 = 𝐗𝐗 ⊤ \mathbf{R}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{X}^{\top} 以限制数值漂移，并为步骤 2 到 4 初始化一个新的 𝐐 = a 2 ​ 𝐈 + b 2 ​ 𝐑 + c 2 ​ 𝐑 2 \mathbf{Q}=a_{2}\mathbf{I}+b_{2}\mathbf{R}+c_{2}\mathbf{R}^{2}。 在 L3 处，核执行调度遵循这些数据依赖关系：方阵状态矩阵乘积核在每个段内执行，而矩形乘积则在相应的方阵状态更新完成后，于重启和最终边界处应用 𝐐 \mathbf{Q}。 为避免冗余计算，对称乘积核计算一个三角形区域，并重复使用每个瓦片的累加器进行原始和转置存储，仅对角线瓦片被写入一次。

paragraphs.en: For each task, we prepare two LLM-judge prompts: one assesses an independently generated written design, and the other assesses generated implementation code. The written design is elicited in a separate agent run described in Section 3.3 . Both judge prompts combine the task description, task-specific design criteria, and shared assessment instructions. These criteria form the design specification, describing the expert’s design choices, the costs they remove, and the requirements for combining them correctly. The design-assessment prompt includes the agent’s written design; the implementation-assessment prompt includes the three levels of guidance, the expert implementation, and the candidate source code. The scoring procedure is described in Section 3.3 .
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个任务，我们准备两个 LLM 评判提示：一个用于评估独立生成的书面设计，另一个用于评估生成的实现代码。 书面设计是在第 3.3 节中描述的单独智能体运行中获得的。 两个评判提示都结合了任务描述、任务特定的设计标准以及通用的评估说明。 这些标准构成了设计规范，描述了专家的设计选择、他们移除的成本以及正确组合这些要素的要求。 设计评估提示包含智能体的书面设计；实现评估提示则包含三个层级的指导、专家的实现方案以及候选源代码。 评分流程在第 3.3 节中有详细说明。

paragraphs.en: Iterative kernel optimization and evaluation. The agent develops candidate implementations by editing the supplied solution.py template shown in Figure 1 (a) . The template specifies the task-specific signature of run(...) and leaves the function body unimplemented; the agent implements this function to produce the required outputs and state updates. The agent interacts with the execution sandbox through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools: read and write support file inspection and implementation editing, bash executes compilation and profiling commands, and submit invokes the evaluator. On submission, the evaluator loads the candidate file and calls run(...) with inputs prepared for each workload according to the task description. The agent uses the returned correctness and timing feedback, together with profiling tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Compute ( ncu ), to diagnose bottlenecks and revise its implementation. This process forms an iterative loop of implementation, compilation, testing, profiling, and revision.
paragraphs.zh: 迭代式内核优化与评估。 智能体通过编辑图 1 (a) 中所示的 provided solution.py 模板，生成候选实现方案。 该模板定义了任务特定的 run(...) 函数签名，但函数体尚未实现；智能体需要实现此函数以生成所需的输出和状态更新。 智能体通过模型上下文协议（MCP）工具与执行沙箱进行交互：读取和写入支持文件以供检查与实现编辑，bash 用于执行编译和性能分析命令，而 submit 则调用评估器。 提交时，评估器会加载候选文件，并根据任务描述为每个工作负载准备输入，然后调用 run(...)。 智能体利用返回的正确性与时序反馈，并结合 NVIDIA Nsight Compute (ncu) 等性能分析工具，诊断性能瓶颈并修订其实现方案。 这一过程构成了一个包含实现、编译、测试、性能分析和修订的迭代循环。

paragraphs.en: Final submission selection. Both runs use the same fixed turn limit and selection procedure. One agent turn consists of a model response requesting one or more tool calls, execution of those calls, and return of their results. A candidate is eligible for final selection only if the candidate passes the correctness and implementation checks and has valid latency measurements on every workload of the task. For each eligible candidate, we compute the geometric mean of its speedups across the task’s workloads, as defined in Section 3.2 . Among eligible candidates produced within the turn limit, we select the one with the highest geometric mean speedup as the final submission.
paragraphs.zh: 最终提交的选择。 两次运行均使用相同的固定回合限制和选择流程。 一次智能体回合包括模型响应以请求一个或多个工具调用、执行这些调用以及返回其结果。 只有当候选项通过正确性和实现检查，并且在任务的所有工作负载上都有有效的延迟测量时，才有资格进入最终选择。 对于每个符合条件的候选项，我们计算其在任务各工作负载上的加速度的几何平均值，具体定义见第 3.2 节。 在回合限制内生成的符合条件的候选项中，我们选择具有最高几何平均加速度的一个作为最终提交。

paragraphs.en: We include an objective evaluation module (shown in Figure 2 ) to check correctness and implementation validity, measure latency, and compute performance scores for submitted implementations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们包含一个客观评估模块（如图 2 所示），用于检查正确性和实现的有效性，测量延迟，并为提交的实现计算性能分数。

paragraphs.en: Correctness and implementation validity. A task is scored as correct only if its submission satisfies both the correctness criteria and implementation requirements on every workload. Violations of the implementation requirements count as incorrect even when numerical outputs are correct. Correctness checks cover numerical outputs, updates to mutable inputs, repeated execution on new inputs, and, where applicable, distributed behavior. We check compliance with the custom-kernel requirements in Section 2.2 using abstract syntax tree (AST) analysis, static keyword scans, and inspection of libraries linked during compilation. For distributed tasks, we inspect communication traffic to verify that the required communication occurs. Manual review and unit tests check compliance with the full task description, including all required outputs and state updates.
paragraphs.zh: 正确性与实现有效性。 仅当提交的作业在所有工作负载上均满足正确性标准和实现要求时，该任务才被判定为正确。 即使数值输出正确，违反实现要求的作业仍被视为不正确。 正确性检查涵盖数值输出、可变输入的更新、在新输入上的重复执行，以及在适用情况下的分布式行为。 我们通过抽象语法树（AST）分析、静态关键字扫描以及对编译时链接的库的检查，来验证对第 2.2 节中自定义内核要求的合规性。 对于分布式任务，我们会检查通信流量，以验证所需的通信是否发生。 通过人工审查和单元测试，可确保完全符合任务描述的所有要求，包括所有必需的输出和状态更新。

paragraphs.en: Execution latency timing. We measure GPU execution time for one call to the candidate run(...) entry point, including its kernels and required communication. Input construction, compilation, and evaluator setup are excluded from the timed region. The evaluator controls input preparation and state restoration to provide equivalent inputs to all implementations. For distributed tasks, the reported latency is the maximum across participating ranks. All implementations of a given workload use the same timing procedure. For tasks with very short kernel execution times, such as decoding, we capture repeated calls to run(...) in a CUDA Graph that takes at least one second to execute and replay the graph five times. For other tasks, we use CUDA events to time batches of repeated calls to run(...) , with each batch lasting at least one second. In both modes, the reported latency is the arithmetic mean of repeated per-call measurements.
paragraphs.zh: 执行延迟计时。 我们测量对候选 run(...) 入口点调用一次的 GPU 执行时间，包括其中的内核和所需的通信操作。 输入构建、编译和评估器设置不包含在计时区域中。 评估器控制输入准备和状态恢复，以确保所有实现都使用等效的输入。 对于分布式任务，报告的延迟是参与计算的各个 rank 中的最大值。 给定工作负载的所有实现均使用相同的计时流程。 对于内核执行时间极短的任务（如解码），我们会将重复调用 run(...) 操作封装到一个 CUDA Graph 中，该图至少需要一秒才能执行，并重复播放该图五次。 对于其他任务，我们使用 CUDA 事件来计时重复调用 run(...) 的批量操作，每个批次的持续时间至少为一秒。 在这两种模式下，报告的延迟均为单次调用重复测量值的算术平均值。

paragraphs.en: The SOL score’s intended interpretation within [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] requires t b , i , w > t SOL , i , w t_{b,i,w}>t_{\mathrm{SOL},i,w} and t i , w ≥ t SOL , i , w t_{i,w}\geq t_{\mathrm{SOL},i,w} . However, D2K-Bench permits algorithmic and dataflow changes that can alter the computation and memory traffic assumed by the bound, so the SOL bound need not remain valid for a generated implementation. For Muon, transformed implementations can execute below the SOL bound derived from the PyTorch reference. paragraphs.en: Implementation assessment. For each task and input configuration, the judge assesses the generated code at L1 (algorithmic insights), L2 (dataflow design), and L3 (low-level optimization), as defined in Section 2.3 . Each level is scored from 0 to 100 using five anchors: absent (0), isolated fragments (25), partial implementation (50), substantial implementation (75), and complete implementation (100). Intermediate scores are permitted, and every score must be supported by exact code passages demonstrating the implemented design choices. Runtime measurements are hidden from the judge. Alternative implementations receive credit when they satisfy the assessed design intent, even if they differ from the expert code. Functional correctness is evaluated separately in Section 3.2 . To include all 26 tasks in implementation comparisons, we assign JS impl m , c , i = 0 \mathrm{JS}_{\text{impl}}^{m,c,i}=0 to an incorrect final submission and set its three level scores to zero. This adjustment uses the separate correctness evaluation, not a runtime-based judgment.

paragraphs.en: We assess whether the LLM judge scores in Section 3.3 align with measured end-to-end kernel performance despite the judge having no access to runtime measurements. Table 2 compares JS design \mathrm{JS}_{\text{design}} for independently proposed designs, JS impl \mathrm{JS}_{\text{impl}} for final implementations, and the measured performance score S perf \mathrm{S}_{\text{perf}} . Each value aggregates the same 26 tasks for a model; implementation and performance scores are reported separately for each guidance configuration. Our key findings are: ( i ) Implementation scores align with performance and guidance gains. In both configurations, JS impl \mathrm{JS}_{\text{impl}} follows the broad model ordering of S perf \mathrm{S}_{\text{perf}} . Guidance also increases both scores for every model. Thus, despite having no runtime access, the judge captures both performance differences across models and the direction of improvement under guidance. paragraphs.en: GPU kernel generation benchmarks. GPU kernel generation benchmarks vary in task and hardware coverage and in the reliability of their evaluation [ 9 ] . KernelBench [ 1 ] established the task of producing a correct GPU kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference; TritonBench [ 10 ] focuses on Triton operators, MultiKernelBench [ 11 ] spans GPUs, NPUs, and TPUs, and DataKernelBench [ 12 ] extends the domain to database queries. Evaluation methods also differ. Robust-kbench [ 13 ] and KernelBench-Verified [ 14 ] strengthen verification and hidden testing, while KernelBenchX [ 15 ] and AgentKernelArena [ 16 ] analyze correctness, hardware efficiency, and agent generalization. SOL-ExecBench [ 5 ] evaluates kernel performance against analytically derived hardware bounds [ 17 ] . FastKernels [ 3 ] emphasizes production interfaces, and RealisticTritonBench [ 18 ] uses framework pull requests and end-to-end tests. FlashInfer-Bench [ 19 ] studies serving workloads, while Atrex-Bench [ 20 ] samples operators and shapes from production inference traces.

AutoKernel [ 21 ] and TritonForge [ 22 ] organize compilation, testing, profiling, and revision, while Astra [ 23 ] and CUDAMaster [ 24 ] add multi-agent or hardware-aware workflows. [6] show that expert directions can improve final implementations in a B200 contest harness. paragraphs.en: We propose D2K-Bench , a new benchmark that measures how effectively LLM agents translate expert design guidance into efficient GPU kernels. The benchmark pairs 26 tasks and 85 workloads with guidance on high-level algorithmic insights, dataflow design, and low-level optimization tricks. Its evaluation combines pairwise performance comparisons with assessments of independently proposed designs and generated code. Across five models on NVIDIA B200 GPUs, guidance raises correctness over 130 model–task pairs from 93.1% to 98.5%. The Performance Score is computed over all 26 tasks for each model and increases from 1.46 to 1.95. Guidance also raises the mean combined implementation score from 57 to 70. Guidance improves performance, but agents still leave assessed design properties unimplemented.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 D2K-Bench，一项新的基准测试，用于衡量 LLM 智能体将专家设计指导转化为高效 GPU 内核的有效性。 该基准测试将 26 个任务和 85 个工作负载与高级算法洞察、数据流设计以及低级优化技巧的指导相结合。 其评估方法结合了成对性能比较，以及对独立提出的设计和生成代码的评估。 在 NVIDIA B200 GPU 上针对五种模型进行测试时，指导使 130 个模型-任务对的正确率从 93.1% 提升至 98.5%。 性能得分基于每个模型的全部 26 个任务计算得出，从 1.46 提升至 1.95。 指导还将平均综合实现得分从 57 提升至 70。 指导提升了性能，但智能体仍未能实现所评估的设计属性。

paragraphs.en: Independent design assessment. The proposal elicited without expert guidance retains the five-step recurrence of the PyTorch reference in Section 2.2 : the proposed method forms an M × M M\times M Gram matrix and writes a new rectangular 𝐗 \mathbf{X} after every coefficient step. The proposal also calls for computing one triangle of symmetric square products and mirroring the off-diagonal tiles. Unlike the expert guidance in Section 2.3 , the proposal neither composes the polynomial actions in 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} nor applies the fixed restart before coefficient 2; the repeated rectangular updates therefore remain. The proposal’s cost argument counts a rectangular Horner multiplication absent from the supplied PyTorch reference and uses 0.26 0.26 for the row-to-column ratio, which is 0.37 0.37 – 0.39 0.39 for the three registered workloads.
paragraphs.zh: 独立的设计评估。 在没有专家指导的情况下提出的方案，保留了第 2.2 节中 PyTorch 参考实现的五步循环：该方法首先构建一个 M × M 的 Gram 矩阵，并在每个系数步骤后写入一个新的矩形矩阵 𝐗 \mathbf{X}。 该方案还要求计算对称平方积的一个三角形区域，并将非对角线元素镜像复制。 与第 2.3 节中的专家指导不同，该方案既没有组合 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} 中的多项式操作，也没有在系数 2 之前应用固定的重启机制；因此，重复的矩形更新仍然存在。 该方案的成本论证中计算了一个在所提供的 PyTorch 参考实现中未出现的矩形霍纳乘法，并将行与列的比例设为 0.26；而对于三个已注册的工作负载，这一比例实际为 0.37 – 0.39。

paragraphs.en: LLM judge assessment. Both assessments use the numerical anchors absent (0), isolated fragments (25), partial (50), substantial (75), and complete (100), with intermediate scores permitted. For the independent proposal, L1 receives 32, between isolated fragments and partial : triangular Gram products provide an algorithmic saving, but the central 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} composition and fixed restart are missing, and the claimed dominant saving is measured against work absent from the PyTorch reference. L2 receives 40, below partial : normalization, the M × M M\times M Gram (the smaller side for these workloads), and buffer reuse are described, but 𝐗 \mathbf{X} is written at every step and no segment-local 𝐑 / 𝐐 \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Q} lifetime or restart handoff is proposed. L3 receives 45, between isolated fragments and partial design : triangular scheduling and mirrored stores are specified, but square-state execution across a composition segment is not. The arithmetic mean of these scores is JS design = 39 \mathrm{JS}_{\text{design}}=39 .
paragraphs.zh: LLM 法官评估。 两次评估均使用以下数值锚点：缺失（0）、孤立片段（25）、部分（50）、实质性（75）和完整（100），并允许中间分数。 对于独立提案，L1 得分为 32，介于孤立片段和部分之间：三角形 Gram 乘积实现了算法上的优化，但核心的 𝐐 \mathbf{Q} 组合与固定重启机制缺失，且所声称的主导性优化效果是相对于 PyTorch 参考实现中未包含的工作而言的。 L2 得分为 40，低于部分水平：归一化、M × M M\times M Gram（在这些工作负载中为较小维度）和缓冲区重用均有描述，但 𝐗 \mathbf{X} 在每一步都被完整写入，且未提出任何分段局部 𝐑 / 𝐐 \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Q} 的生命周期管理或重启交接方案。 L3 得分为 45，介于孤立片段和部分设计之间：三角形调度和镜像存储均有说明，但跨组合段的方形状态执行则未被提及。 这些分数的算术平均值为 JS 设计 = 39 \mathrm{JS}_{\text{design}}=39 。
